subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose these lifecycle boundaries through HOOK.md workspace/internal hooks, through typed plugin hooks only, or through a split surface with different payload and permission levels?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing this API affects extension boundaries, trusted local automation, session-state exposure, and possible new config semantics.

options.title: Split workspace observation from plugin control
options.body: Expose a minimal observation-only workspace event such as subagent:ended while keeping richer turn/tool lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks with documented permissions.

options.title: Use typed plugin hooks only
options.body: Keep HOOK.md hooks for coarse operator automation and require lifecycle, memory, and learning systems to use the plugin API.

options.title: Add the full workspace lifecycle surface
options.body: Add subagent, turn-complete, and threshold workspace events after maintainers define payloads, ordering, and config semantics.

recommendation.title: Split workspace observation from plugin control
recommendation.body: Expose a minimal observation-only workspace event such as subagent:ended while keeping richer turn/tool lifecycle control in typed plugin hooks with documented permissions.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security boundary choice and steipete has recent adjacent core subagent ownership plus direct issue discussion routing.
